title: Cohomology of Quasi Coherent Sheaves on Affine and Projective Schemes

items.title: Enough injective sheaves of modules
items.statement: For every ringed space (X,O_X), the abelian category Mod(O_X) has enough injectives under AC, so a supplied injective resolution can be chosen for each O_X-module.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The category of O_X-modules has all colimits and filtered colimits are exact on stalks. For each open U, the extension by zero of the free rank-one O_U-module represents sections on U; a sum over the set of opens forms a generator because a nonzero sheaf has a nonzero local section. Thus Mod(O_X) is a locally small Grothendieck category. Apply the published functorial injective embedding construction under AC and iterate cokernels. This proves the injectives needed for O-module, not merely abelian-sheaf, derived pushforward.

items.title: Higher direct image of a sheaf
items.statement: Assume AC, which supplies functorial injective resolutions of O_X-modules and implies the DC hypotheses of derived-functor comparison. For a ringed-space morphism f:X→S and an O_X-module F, define R^q f_*F as H^q(f_*I(F)_del) for the fixed functorial resolution datum; R^0 f_*F is canonically f_*F, q<0 gives zero, and another supplied datum gives a canonical comparison isomorphism.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.title: Local-section formula for derived direct image
items.statement: For a morphism f:X→S of schemes and an O_X-module F, R^qf_*F is the sheafification of the presheaf V↦H^q(f^{-1}V,F|f^{-1}V) on S for q≥0; the formula respects restrictions and its O_S-module structure.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Let F→I^• be an injective resolution in O_X-modules. An injective O_X-module I is flasque as an underlying abelian sheaf: for W⊂V, the natural injection j_{W!}O_W→j_{V!}O_V lets injectivity lift a section on W to V. Restrictions I|f^{-1}V remain flasque, so their global sections are cohomologically acyclic; the restricted resolution therefore computes H^q(f^{-1}V,F). The terms of f_*I^• have sections Γ(f^{-1}V,I^p), and cohomology sheaves are the sheafifications of the presheaf cohomology of this complex. The latter presheaf cohomology is exactly the asserted H^q by the flasque argument. Restriction maps and O_S scalar action descend from the complex. This is the standard proof behind Stacks Cohomology of Schemes §30.4.

items.title: Exact principal-open Čech resolution
items.statement: For A a ring, M an A-module, and f_1,…,f_r generating 1, the augmented alternating Čech complex 0→M→⊕M_{f_i}→⊕M_{f_if_j}→⋯ is exact; this also holds after localizing A and M at any element.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Identify each intersection D(f_{i_0})∩⋯∩D(f_{i_p}) with Spec A_{f_{i_0}⋯f_{i_p}} and its section module with M localized there. Localize the augmented complex at a prime p; pick i with f_i∉p, then inserting i with the Čech sign defines a contracting homotopy. Exactness of a complex of A-modules is detected at all prime localizations. This proves the full complex, not merely the degree-zero equalizer. AC supplies prime existence for the local detection step.

items.title: Affine acyclicity of quasi-coherent sheaves
items.statement: For every affine scheme X=Spec A and quasi-coherent O_X-module F, H^q(X,F)=0 for every q>0, including the empty affine scheme.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Use the distinguished affine opens as a basis containing X and closed under intersections. Finite standard principal covers are cofinal in covers of any such open by quasi-compactness. The previous exact augmented module Čech complex gives positive Čech vanishing for each standard cover, with F|D(g) identified with a localized module. Apply the published cofinal-basis acyclicity theorem with its actual hypotheses. This avoids assuming acyclicity of intersections before proving it.

items.title: Acyclic intersections of principal affine opens
items.statement: For a finite standard cover of Spec A by D(f_i), every nonempty finite intersection is Spec A_{∏f_i}; the restriction of every quasi-coherent F to it has no positive sheaf cohomology.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The intersection identity is the distinguished-open localization identity; include zero and empty intersections as Spec 0. Restriction of quasi-coherent sheaves remains quasi-coherent by the affine-cover criterion. Apply the preceding affine acyclicity theorem separately to each intersection.

items.title: Cech cohomology computes quasi-coherent cohomology on a separated scheme
items.statement: If X is quasi-compact and separated and U_0,…,U_r is a finite affine open cover, then every finite intersection is affine and, for every quasi-coherent F, the canonical comparison H^q(C^•(U,F))→H^q(X,F) is an isomorphism for all q.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: For affine U,V⊂X, identify U∩V with the inverse image of affine U×V under the diagonal X→X×X. Separation makes the diagonal a closed immersion, so its inverse image is affine by the local quotient characterization. Induct over finite intersections, then apply affine acyclicity to F on each. Choose the finite ordering of the cover and invoke the published Leray acyclic-cover theorem; the complex uses the same alternating signs as its statement.

items.title: Higher direct images of quasi-coherent modules vanish along affine morphisms
items.statement: For an affine scheme morphism f:X→S and quasi-coherent F on X, R^qf_*F=0 for all q>0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: For an affine V⊂S, f^{-1}V is affine and F restricts to a quasi-coherent sheaf, so H^q(f^{-1}V,F)=0. By the local-section formula, the sheafification of V↦H^q(f^{-1}V,F) is R^qf_*F; this presheaf vanishes on the affine basis for q>0. Since affine V form a basis, all positive direct-image cohomology sheaves vanish.

items.title: Cohomology of an affine morphism and its pushforward
items.statement: If f:X→S is affine and F is quasi-coherent, the natural maps H^q(S,f_*F)→H^q(X,F) are isomorphisms for every q≥0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Resolve F by its Godement flasque resolution G^•. Each f_*G^p is flasque, since restriction on S is restriction on inverse images and G^p is flasque. The cohomology sheaf of f_*G^• is R^qf_*F and vanishes for q>0 by the previous theorem, so f_*G^• is a flasque resolution of f_*F. Its global sections equal Γ(X,G^•), giving identical cohomology in every degree; identify the resulting map with the natural edge map.

items.title: Closed immersion preserves cohomology and coherent pushforward
items.statement: For a closed immersion i:Z→X and quasi-coherent F on Z, H^q(Z,F)≅H^q(X,i_*F) for all q. If X is locally Noetherian and F coherent, i_*F is coherent.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: A closed immersion is affine: on Spec A its inverse image is Spec(A/I). Apply the preceding affine cohomology isomorphism. On that chart, a coherent F corresponds to a finite A/I-module, hence to a finite A-module; the associated direct-image sheaf is coherent because A is Noetherian. Check naturality on overlaps.

items.title: Twist of a quasi-coherent sheaf
items.statement: For projective X with the specified invertible O_X(1) from a fixed projective embedding, define F(d)=F⊗O_X(d) for every d∈Z. For a general ample L write F⊗L^d; the notation F(d) does not silently switch the embedding.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.title: Laurent-monomial decomposition of the projective Čech complex
items.statement: For S=A[x_0,…,x_n] and its standard cover of P^n_A, the Čech complex for O(d) is the direct sum over exponent vectors e∈Z^{n+1} with Σe_i=d of complexes indexed by subsets containing N(e)={i:e_i<0}. Each summand has H^0=A when N(e)=∅, H^n=A when N(e) is all indices, and zero otherwise, with the n=0 overlap interpreted in degree zero.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: On D_+(x_{i_0}⋯x_{i_p}), degree-d sections are Laurent monomials whose negative exponents occur only among the inverted variables. The alternating differential preserves each exponent vector. If N(e)=∅, the summand is the full simplex complex, giving H^0=A. If N(e) is all vertices, only the top intersection contributes. For nonempty proper N(e), choose a vertex outside N(e) and contract by inserting it with its Čech sign. Direct sums commute with cohomology of module complexes; treat n=0 separately where both descriptions of the single term coincide.

items.title: Cohomology of O(d) on projective space
items.statement: For any ring A, n≥0, and d∈Z, H^q(P^n_A,O(d)) vanishes unless q=0 or q=n. If n>0, H^0 is A[x_0,…,x_n]_d for d≥0 and zero for d<0; H^n is free on Laurent monomials x_0^{e_0}⋯x_n^{e_n} with every e_i<0 and Σe_i=d, hence nonzero precisely for d≤−n−1 when A≠0. For n=0, P^0_A=Spec A and H^0(O(d))≅A for every d, with all higher groups zero.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Apply the monomial-summand lemma and sum the surviving degree-zero and degree-n weights. Count degree-d nonnegative exponent vectors and the all-negative vectors. In the n=0 case the standard cover has one affine member and O(d) is canonically free rank one, so its unique cohomology group is A in degree zero for every d. Include the zero-ring convention: the displayed free module can be zero even in a nominally nonzero range.

items.title: Global sections of projective twists
items.statement: For n>0, H^0(P^n_A,O(d)) is A[x_0,…,x_n]_d if d≥0 and zero if d<0; for n=0 it is A for every d.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Take the degree-zero case of the full computation, retaining the exceptional n=0 case. The identification is the monomial basis of homogeneous polynomials.

items.title: Intermediate cohomology of projective twists vanishes
items.statement: For n≥0 and every d, H^q(P^n_A,O(d))=0 for 0<q<n.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The Laurent-monomial summands have cohomology only in degrees zero and n. If n≤1 the stated index range is empty, so no contradictory case appears.

items.title: Top cohomology of projective twists
items.statement: For n≥0, the top cohomology of O(d) on P^n_A is A when n=0; when n≥1 it is free on all-negative Laurent monomials of total degree d, zero for d>−n−1 and of rank binomial(−d−1,n) when d≤−n−1 and A≠0 (zero for A=0).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Read off the all-negative exponent vectors from the theorem. Substitute a_i=−e_i−1≥0 to count solutions Σa_i=−d−n−1. State n=0 separately because top and degree-zero cohomology coincide.

items.title: Projective n-space has quasi-coherent cohomological dimension at most n
items.statement: For any ring A, every quasi-coherent F on P^n_A satisfies H^q(P^n_A,F)=0 for q>n; this includes n=0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The n+1 standard affine opens have affine finite intersections. Their alternating Čech complex ends in degree n, so its cohomology vanishes above n. Invoke the comparison theorem for arbitrary quasi-coherent F; n=0 is affine acyclicity.

items.title: Dimension bound for quasi-coherent cohomology on a Noetherian scheme
items.statement: If X is a separated Noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension d≥0, H^q(X,F)=0 for every quasi-coherent F and every q>d. The empty scheme has no positive cohomology.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The underlying space of a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian and its topological chain dimension agrees with scheme Krull dimension. Apply the published Grothendieck vanishing theorem for all abelian sheaves to the underlying abelian sheaf of F. Separation is retained from the design although the cited topological theorem is stronger. Handle X empty by the terminal section convention.

items.title: Eventual generation of coherent projective twists
items.statement: Let X be projective over a Noetherian ring A, let L be an ample invertible sheaf on X, and let F be coherent. Then F⊗L^m is globally generated for all sufficiently large m, with a bound depending on F.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: A projective scheme over Noetherian A is Noetherian. Apply the batch-8 Serre criterion for ampleness, whose statement is exactly eventual global generation for every coherent F. Verify L is absolute ample on X; if L comes from an embedding into P^N_A, use batch-8 very-ample-implies-ample over affine base. This lemma records the finite generating sections used in the cohomological induction.

items.title: Projective coherent finiteness and large twist vanishing
items.statement: For a Noetherian ring A and coherent G on P^n_A, each H^q(P^n_A,G) is finite over A and H^q(P^n_A,G(m))=0 for q>0 and all sufficiently large m. The same holds for a closed projective subscheme with O(1).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Use global generation of a sufficiently high twist to obtain a finite surjection E=⊕O(a_j)→G and coherent kernel K. Descend on q from q>n, where the Čech bound gives zero. In 0→K(m)→E(m)→G(m)→0, H^q(E(m)) and H^{q+1}(K(m)) vanish for q>0 and m large by the explicit O(a_j+m) computation and induction. The same long exact segment, with finite A-modules on either side, proves H^q(G) finite; Noetherianity makes kernels and cokernels finite. For closed X⊂P^n_A, i_*F is coherent by the closed-immersion lemma and its cohomology agrees with F; projection formula for the invertible O(1) follows chartwise from restriction of graded shifts.

items.title: Serre vanishing for coherent sheaves and ample twists
items.statement: Let X be projective over a Noetherian ring A, let F be coherent, and let L be ample on X. Then H^q(X,F⊗L^m)=0 for every q>0 and every sufficiently large integer m, simultaneously in q.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Choose d>0 so L^d is the pullback of O(1) along a closed embedding X→P^N_A, using the batch-8 ample-powers theorem with properness of X. For each residue r∈{0,…,d−1}, apply the preceding projective-space lemma to the coherent i_*(F⊗L^r). Its positive cohomology vanishes after n high O(1)-twists; closed-immersion cohomology identifies this with H^q(X,F⊗L^{dn+r}). Take the maximum of finitely many bounds for r and q≤N. The conclusion does not require a hyperplane avoiding associated points over a finite field.

items.title: Higher direct images localize over an affine base
items.statement: If f:X→S is quasi-compact and separated and F is quasi-coherent, then R^qf_*F is quasi-coherent. For any affine V=Spec A⊂S, (R^qf_*F)|V is associated to H^q(f^{-1}V,F); on D(a)⊂V its sections are the localization H^q(f^{-1}V,F)_a.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Choose a finite affine cover of f^{-1}V. Separation makes every finite intersection affine; its coordinate ring and F-sections localize after the base change V→D(a). Consequently the finite alternating Čech complex for f^{-1}D(a) is the localization of the complex over V. Localization is exact, so H^q localizes. The presheaf of cohomology on affine V therefore has the module localization property and sheafifies to an associated quasi-coherent module; compare with the injective-resolution definition of R^qf_* by the standard local-section formula. This is the local compatibility needed for proper direct-image coherence.

items.title: Affine neighbourhood containing component generic points
items.statement: On a quasi-separated Noetherian scheme X with finitely many irreducible components of generic points η_1,…,η_r, every point x has an affine open neighbourhood also containing all η_i.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Let η_1,…,η_s be generics of components containing x. Choose an affine W containing x and avoiding the remaining components; it contains η_1,…,η_s. For each remaining generic choose an affine neighbourhood U_i, arranged pairwise disjoint by shrinking around points whose closures are distinct components. The quasi-compact intersections W∩U_i avoid η_i; shrink each U_i by a principal open about η_i disjoint from W∩U_i, using the finite-cover prime-avoidance argument. The resulting W and U_i are disjoint affines, so their finite union is affine and contains x and all generics. This spells out Stacks Tag 01ZX and the quasi-separatedness use.

items.title: Schematic closure and agreement on a dense open
items.statement: For a quasi-compact open immersion j:U→Y with Y Noetherian, ker(O_Y→j_*O_U) is a quasi-coherent ideal defining the schematic closure Z⊂Y; U→Z is schematically dense and open. If two morphisms Z→T into a separated target agree on U, they agree on Z.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: On each affine V=Spec A with finite affine/principal cover of U∩V, compute the kernel of A→Γ(U∩V,O_U); localization on V shows the kernels glue as a quasi-coherent ideal. Quotient by it makes O_Z→j_*O_U injective, the definition of schematic density, while U remains an open subscheme. The equalizer of two T-valued maps is the inverse image of T’s closed diagonal. Its ideal vanishes on U, so injectivity O_Z→j_*O_U forces that ideal to vanish on Z. Use this argument instead of the published schematic-image theorem whose published prerequisite chain has a recorded associated-module gap.

items.title: Projective-space projection is universally closed by finite graded pieces
items.statement: For every scheme S and n≥0, the projection P^n_S→S is universally closed; for every S-scheme T and every closed subset Z⊂P^n_T, its image in T is closed.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Base change of P^n_S is P^n_T, and closedness is local on T, so take T=Spec B. By the Proj topology write the closed subset as V_+(I) for a homogeneous ideal I⊂B[x_0,…,x_n]. For p∈Spec B, the fibre is empty exactly when the irrelevant ideal in κ(p)[x]/Iκ(p) is nilpotent, equivalently every degree-d monomial belongs to Iκ(p) for some d>0; one direction uses homogeneous-prime existence under AC, and the finite monomial count gives a common d. The degree-d quotient M_d=(B[x]/I)_d is finite over B, so this is M_d⊗κ(p)=0. Local Nakayama gives (M_d)_p=0, and finite generation yields b∉p with (M_d)_b=0. Every fibre over D(b) is empty, so the complement of the image is open. This holds after arbitrary T→S and includes n=0 and the zero ring. Vakil §§8.4.7–8.4.8 gives the graded elimination route but leaves its final arbitrary-base step as an exercise; the finite-module/Nakayama step above completes that gap.

items.title: Affine finite-type source immerses into relative projective space
items.statement: Assuming AC, any affine scheme U locally of finite type over any scheme S admits an S-immersion into P^N_S for some finite N, including U=empty.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 29.40.3 (Tag 01VS), affine-source case

items.strategy: Cover U by finitely many principal opens over affine base opens; descend finite algebra generators, clear denominators to global sections of O_U, obtain a projective map and show it is a closed immersion over a covering family of target opens.

items.title: Chow lemma for proper Noetherian schemes
items.statement: Let S be Noetherian and f:X→S separated and of finite type. There is a proper surjective π:X′→X and an S-immersion X′→P^N_S for some finite N; there is a dense open U⊂X with π^{-1}(U)≅U; the construction passes through its schematic closure in X. If f is proper, the immersion is closed, so X′ is projective over S.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Cover X by finitely many affine U_i each containing all component generics; their intersection U is dense. Replace X by the schematic closure of U, a surjective closed subscheme agreeing on U, to make U schematically dense. Immerse each affine U_i into some finite P^{n_i}_S using finite-type generators, then take its schematic closure Z_i there. Take the schematic closure Z of U diagonally inside the product of the Z_i, which is projective over S via finite Segre embeddings. Derive properness of each projective ambient without the batch-5 projective-properness theorem: finite standard charts give finite type, the local affine quotient argument makes the relative diagonal closed, and the immediately preceding independent graded-piece lemma supplies universal closedness. Over each U_i set V_i=p_i^{-1}(U_i); the proper maps V_i→U_i agree on overlaps because they agree on schematically dense U and X is separated. They glue to π on V=∪V_i. The same schematic-density plus closed-image argument gives π^{-1}(U_i)=V_i, so π is proper locally on X, and π^{-1}(U)=U. Every fibre over U_i is covered, hence π is surjective. This proves the separated finite-type form of Chow. If X→S is proper, π makes X′=V proper over S; its immersion into separated P^N_S is proper by the proper-source-to-separated-target lemma and has closed image, hence is a closed immersion. The argument uses no proof path through the published affine-closed-immersion theorem circular citation. Check each image/closure and triple overlap in the authored proof; cite Stacks §30.18 only as backing, not as the argument.

items.title: Noetherian dévissage for coherent proper pushforward
items.statement: Assume AC. For a Noetherian scheme X and a coherent-sheaf property P with P(0) and two-out-of-three, if every integral closed Z with generic ξ has a coherent witness G supported on Z with m_ξG_ξ=0, dim_{κ(ξ)}G_ξ=1, and P(G), then all coherent sheaves on X have P.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Noetherian induction on minimal counterexample support. Split reducible support using a power of one component ideal, filter irreducible support by the reduced ideal, and compare each integral-scheme quotient with direct sums of the generic witness through a common coherent subsheaf formed inside a quasi-coherent finite-open pushforward. All error kernels and quotients have smaller support. This proves Stacks 01YH scope without an external coherent-extension lemma.

items.title: Coherent higher direct images under proper morphisms
items.statement: Let f:X→S be proper with S locally Noetherian and F coherent on X. Then R^qf_*F is coherent on S for every q≥0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Work on affine Noetherian V⊂S, where coherence of R^q is equivalent to finite A-module cohomology by the localization lemma. Let P(F) mean all R^qf_*F coherent; long exact direct images and coherence of kernels/cokernels make P two-out-of-three. For each integral closed Z⊂X, Chow lemma gives a projective π:Z′→Z isomorphic over a dense open, with Z′ projective over V. Choose π-relatively ample L from the projective embedding. Relative Serre vanishing, proved by the projective-space induction on finite affine base covers, makes R^{>0}π_*L^m=0 and R^{>0}(f|Z∘π)_*L^m=0 for m≫0. Set G=π_*L^m, push it to X; it is coherent by the already proved projective case, has one-dimensional generic fibre, and Leray’s finite-first-quadrant derived-composition argument identifies R^{>0}(f|Z)_*G=0 and degree zero with a coherent projective pushforward. Apply the dévissage lemma to conclude P for all F. The proof must display the proper, projective, and generic-rank hypotheses at each step; no proper-to-projective shortcut is assumed.

items.title: Finite coherent cohomology for proper schemes
items.statement: If A is Noetherian, X→Spec A is proper and F is coherent, then H^q(X,F) is a finite A-module for every q; moreover H^q(X,F)=0 for all sufficiently large q.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The proper pushforward theorem makes R^qf_*F coherent; on affine Spec A its sections are H^q(X,F) by the localization lemma, so these modules are finite. X is quasi-compact and separated, so choose a finite affine cover with affine intersections; its bounded Čech complex gives vanishing above the number of opens minus one. A Noetherian base ring may have infinite Krull dimension, so the finite-cover argument is essential here. The title retains “projective” from the design but the conclusion has the stated proper scope.

items.title: Finite-dimensional coherent cohomology over a field
items.statement: If X is proper over a field k and F is coherent, every H^q(X,F) is finite-dimensional over k and only finitely many q are nonzero.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Apply the proper-over-Noetherian-ring theorem with A=k; finite k-modules are finite-dimensional vector spaces. Retain the finite affine-cover cohomological bound for the Euler sum.

items.title: Euler characteristic of a coherent sheaf
items.statement: For proper X/k and coherent F, define χ(X,F)=Σ_{q≥0}(−1)^q dim_k H^q(X,F); the sum is finite by proper coherent finiteness and vanishing. For the empty scheme set χ=0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.title: Euler characteristic is additive
items.statement: For 0→F′→F→F″→0 of coherent sheaves on proper X/k, χ(X,F)=χ(X,F′)+χ(X,F″).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The long exact cohomology sequence consists of finite-dimensional spaces and vanishes above a common finite bound. Break it into finite short exact pieces or take alternating dimensions of the full exact sequence; connecting terms cancel. The zero sheaf and empty scheme contribute zero.

items.title: Hilbert function and Euler characteristic on a projective scheme
items.statement: For projective X/k with fixed O_X(1) and coherent F, define h_F(m)=dim_k H^0(X,F(m)) for m∈Z and P_F(m)=χ(X,F(m)). They need not agree before Serre vanishing; when P_F is polynomial it is the Hilbert polynomial.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.title: High-degree section module is finite graded
items.statement: For coherent F on P^n_k, the truncated graded module ⊕_{m≥m_0} H^0(P^n_k,F(m)) is finite over k[x_0,…,x_n] for sufficiently large m_0; the same holds after extension by zero from any projective closed subscheme.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Use eventual global generation and Serre vanishing to give finitely generated graded sections by degrees, prove exactness with the long exact sheaf cohomology sequence, and control tails by nonnegative shifts of the polynomial graded ring.

items.title: Flat field extension commutes with coherent cohomology
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the proper finiteness corollary
and the Čech comparison cited below ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a
field ([[def-field]]), let $K/k$ be a field extension, let $X$ be a scheme
proper over $k$ ([[def-proper-morphism]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]). Form the base change
$X_K:=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ with projection
$g:X_K\to X$, and put $\mathcal F_K:=g^*\mathcal F$
([[def-pullback-module-ringed-spaces]]); then $X_K$ is proper over $K$ and
$\mathcal F_K$ is coherent, so both sides below are finite-dimensional by the
corollary cited in [F7].

Then $\kappa^q$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$, where
$$\kappa^q:H^q(X,\mathcal F)\otimes_kK\longrightarrow H^q(X_K,\mathcal F_K)$$
is the natural map of the statement: the base-change map of
[[def-base-change-map-cohomology]] for the Cartesian square over
$\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which on global sections is the
$K$-linear extension of the pullback of cohomology classes along $g$
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]).

In particular, writing $\chi$ for the Euler characteristic
([[def-euler-characteristic-coherent-sheaf]]),
$$\chi(X_K,\mathcal F_K)=\chi(X,\mathcal F).$$

The empty scheme $X=\varnothing$, the zero sheaf $\mathcal F=0$, the degree
$q=0$ and the trivial extension $K=k$ are included; $k$ needs to be neither
perfect nor infinite, and $K/k$ need not be separable, finite or algebraic.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Choose a finite affine cover of separated proper X with affine intersections. Its base change to K has the same nerve and affine intersections. On every term, sections of F_K are the old sections tensored with K by affine module base change. Since K is flat over k, tensor commutes with cohomology of the finite Čech complex. Dimensions of the finite-dimensional groups are unchanged. This supplies the descent from an arbitrary field to an infinite or algebraically closed extension in the hyperplane argument.

items.title: Support dimension under field extension
items.statement: For a finite-type k-scheme X, coherent F, and field extension K/k, dim Supp(F_K)=dim Supp(F), with the empty support convention.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Use a finite affine cover and reduce support to Spec of finite-type quotients by annihilator ideals. On each irreducible component choose a Noether normalization by a polynomial subring in d variables; its finite module extension remains finite after tensoring with K. The map K[T_1,…,T_d] into the base-changed algebra remains injective by faithful flatness, and finite integral extension preserves dimension d. Faithful flatness keeps nonempty support nonempty; take the maximum dimension over components and charts. Take the maximum over the finite cover and components; empty support remains empty.

items.title: Regular hyperplane step for coherent support induction
items.statement: Let k be infinite, X⊂P^n_k projective, and 0≠F coherent. There is a linear form ℓ avoiding every associated point of F, so multiplication F(m−1)→F(m) is injective for every m, with coherent cokernel G(m) supported on Supp(F)∩V(ℓ). If dim Supp(F)=d≥1, then dim Supp(G)=d−1; if d=0, ℓ can be chosen invertible on Supp(F) and G=0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Cover X by finitely many projective affine charts; the associated points of coherent F form a finite set. Each point imposes a proper linear subspace of linear forms vanishing there, so over infinite k choose ℓ outside their union. On a local trivialization of O(1), ℓ avoids the associated primes of F_x and is a nonzerodivisor, proving injection. The quotient is supported precisely where ℓ vanishes on Supp(F), checked by Nakayama at those points. Each positive-dimensional irreducible component is cut properly by ℓ; after passing to its reduced structure and to an algebraic closure, use the projective hypersurface dimension-drop lemma, then descend dimension by faithfully flat field extension. Zero-dimensional support is a finite set avoided by ℓ, so the quotient vanishes.

items.title: Euler characteristic is a Hilbert polynomial
items.statement: For projective X/k with fixed embedding and coherent F, there is a unique polynomial P_F(t)∈Q[t] such that P_F(m)=χ(X,F(m)) for every integer m. For m≫0 it also equals h_F(m). The zero sheaf has polynomial zero.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The finite graded section module and published Hilbert–Serre theorem give eventual polynomiality of h_F over the field k, while Serre vanishing makes h_F(m)=χ(F(m)) for m≫0. To prove equality for every integer, extend to an infinite field without changing χ, select the regular hyperplane of the preceding lemma, and use 0→F(m−1)→F(m)→G(m)→0. By induction on support dimension, χ(G(m)) is a polynomial valid for all m; therefore the finite difference χ(F(m))−χ(F(m−1)) is polynomial for all m. A discrete antiderivative over Q is polynomial, and the eventual values fix its additive constant, hence every integer value. For dimension zero the quotient G vanishes, so χ(F(m)) is constant. Do not identify χ with h0 before the stated large-twist bound.

items.title: Degree of the coherent Hilbert polynomial
items.statement: For nonzero coherent F on a projective X/k, deg P_F=dim Supp(F), with the convention deg 0=−∞ for F=0 and dim∅=−∞.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: After extending k to an infinite algebraically closed field, dimensions and the Hilbert polynomial remain unchanged. Induct on d=dim Supp(F). For d=0, F has finite nonempty support, positive cohomology vanishes and twisting by an invertible sheaf preserves each local length; thus P_F is a positive constant. For d≥1, the regular hyperplane exact sequence gives ΔP_F=P_G, and the preceding lemma gives dim Supp(G)=d−1. By induction P_G has exact degree d−1 with positive leading coefficient; the finite-difference operator lowers degree exactly one, so P_F has degree d. The support and dimension under extension are checked on projective charts; no positivity claim for F=0. AC is used to choose an algebraic closure for the reduction.

items.title: Sections of a sheaf flat over the base are flat over affine opens
items.statement: Let f:X→S be a morphism of schemes and F a quasi-coherent O_X-module flat over S (every stalk F_x flat over O_{S,f(x)}). For affine opens U=Spec B ⊆ X and V=Spec A ⊆ S with f(U)⊆V, the A-module F(U) is flat. (Local supplier added in Step 3b; consumes the Stacks Project Lemma 29.26.2, Tag 01U4.)

references.title: The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 29.26.2 (Tag 01U4)
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.39.18 (Tag 00HT)

items.strategy: Local supplier for the proper flat base-change lemma. Reduce to the affine situation: on the affine U=Spec B the restriction of the quasi-coherent F is the sheaf associated to M=F(U), with stalks M_q; at a prime q with p=q∩A flatness of F over S reads M_q flat over A_p. Test flatness of M over A with the ideal criterion: for a finitely generated ideal I ⊆ A with kernel K of I⊗_A M → M, if K ≠ 0 then a maximal ideal m ⊆ B with K_m ≠ 0 exists, and localizing at m turns the kernel into the kernel of I_{p_0}⊗M_m → M_m, which vanishes because M_m is flat over A_{p_0}; contradiction. No finiteness or flatness of A→B is needed; AC enters only through the maximal-ideal zero criterion.

items.title: Finite projective complex for proper flat coherent cohomology
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian, f:X→Spec A proper, and F coherent and flat over A. There is a bounded complex K^• of finite projective A-modules whose cohomology after every ring map A→A′ naturally computes H^q(X_{A′},F_{A′}) in all degrees q. It can be made finite free locally on Spec A.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Take a finite affine cover of X with affine intersections and its bounded alternating Čech complex C^•. Every term is A-flat because F is flat over A, and after any A→A′ its tensor is the Čech complex for the pulled-back cover, so it universally computes fibre/base-change cohomology. Proper coherent finiteness makes H^q(C) finite A-modules. Over Noetherian A, build a bounded-above finite free complex mapping quasi-isomorphically to C by descending through degrees and choosing finite generators of each cohomology and relation kernel; Noetherianity keeps the kernels finite. Because every Čech term is A-flat and the complex is concentrated in a fixed finite range, C⊗_A M has cohomology only in that range for every A-module M; this is finite Tor amplitude of the represented derived object. A bounded-above finite-free replacement exists because C has finite cohomology over the Noetherian ring. Dimension shift using the universal Tor bound makes a sufficiently remote finite syzygy projective; split the free tail to obtain a bounded finite-projective replacement. This is the algebra behind Stacks §30.22 Lemma 22.1 and Vakil §28.2.1–3; the author must display the syzygy/Tor argument, not merely cite perfectness.

items.title: Finite-stage descent of finitely presented schemes and their morphisms
items.statement: Under AC, for a filtered ring system A=colim A_i, every finite-presentation A-scheme descends to a finite-presentation stage; morphisms between fixed stages descend and their equalities are eventual. Finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness; empty schemes and nonflat transitions are included.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Limits of Schemes, Lemma 32.10.1 (Tag 01ZM)
The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Definition 29.22.1 and Lemma 29.22.2 (Tags 01TP and 01TQ)

items.strategy: Descend finite polynomial presentations, quasi-compact principal-open covers, affine gluing isomorphisms and their finite cocycle equations. Descend scheme maps on finite principal refinements and enforce eventual equality on target overlap charts. Source-checked against Stacks Tag 01ZM.

items.title: Finite-stage descent of finitely presented quasi-coherent sheaves
items.statement: Under AC, for a finite-presentation stage scheme X_i over A_i, every finitely presented quasi-coherent module on its limit base change descends to a finitely presented module at a later stage; maps and equalities between fixed stage modules descend. Empty and zero cases and nonflat transitions are included.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Limits of Schemes, Lemma 32.10.2 (Tag 01ZR)
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.127.6, finite-presentation module maps under filtered colimits

items.strategy: Use finite matrix presentations and the filtered-colimit Hom lemma on a finite affine cover; descend overlap maps, inverses, cocycles and morphisms on finite principal refinements. Source-checked against Stacks Tag 01ZR.

items.title: Finite-stage descent of relative flatness for a finitely presented sheaf
items.statement: Under AC, for a directed system of finite-type Z-algebras and a finite-presentation stage scheme with a finitely presented quasi-coherent sheaf, flatness of the limit sheaf over the limit base holds at some finite stage. Empty/zero cases and nonflat transitions are included.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Limits of Schemes, Lemma 32.10.4 (Tag 05LY)
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.168.1(3) (Tag 02JO)

items.strategy: Apply the current local Noetherian approximation and eventual-flatness suppliers at every limit prime; open the stage flat locus, take a finite principal cover of each limit affine chart, and make its unit-ideal coverage hold at a later stage. Source-checked against Stacks Tags 05LY and 02JO.

items.title: Finite-stage descent of properness for finitely presented schemes
items.statement: Under AC, for a filtered system of finite-type Z-algebras, a finite-presentation stage morphism whose limit base change is proper becomes proper after passage to a finite stage. Transition maps need not be flat or injective; the empty source is included.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Limits of Schemes, Lemma 32.13.1 (Tag 081F)
The Stacks Project, Coherent Cohomology, Lemma 30.18.1 (Tag 0200)

items.strategy: Descend the closed-immersion property by finite quotient-ideal generators, apply it to the diagonal for separatedness, use the locally proved Noetherian Chow projective cover and descend its closed limit immersion, then prove universal closedness through the proper surjective cover. Source-checked against Stacks Tag 081F.

items.title: Noetherian approximation of proper flat finitely presented sheaf data
items.statement: Under AC, a proper finite-presentation X over any ring A with a finitely presented A-flat sheaf descends to a proper finite-presentation model and flat finitely presented sheaf over a finitely generated Z-subalgebra of A, including empty and zero cases.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2
The Stacks Project, Derived Categories of Schemes, §§36.26–36.32
The Stacks Project, Limits of Schemes, §§32.8–32.13
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.168.1

items.strategy: Write A as a filtered union of finite-type Z-subalgebras. Apply the locally proved finite-stage scheme, sheaf, properness and relative-flatness carriers in sequence; combine their finite stage enlargements. The carriers prove the Stacks 01ZM/01ZR/081F/05LY scope internally, so no external limit assertion remains load-bearing.

items.title: Universal finite projective cohomology complex over any base
items.statement: For any ring A, proper finite-presentation f:X→Spec A, and finitely presented A-flat F, there is a bounded complex K of finite projective A-modules such that H^q(K⊗_A A′)≅H^q(X_{A′},F_{A′}) naturally for every A-algebra A′. Locally on Spec A it is finite free.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2
The Stacks Project, Derived Categories of Schemes, §§36.26–36.32

items.strategy: Choose Noetherian-stage data (A_i,X_i,F_i) from the preceding approximation lemma. Apply the Noetherian proper-flat finite-complex lemma to obtain K_i, finite projective over A_i and computing cohomology for every A_i-algebra. Put K=K_i⊗_{A_i}A, which is bounded finite projective. For each A-algebra A′, transitivity identifies K⊗_A A′ with K_i⊗_{A_i}A′ and the descended geometric base change X_i×A′ with X×A′; the Noetherian-stage universal computation gives the result. Since finite projective modules are Zariski locally free, K is finite free near each point. This reconstructs Stacks Derived Categories of Schemes §36.30 Lemma 30.1 and Remark 30.2 from explicit Noetherian approximation.

items.title: Cohomology and base-change map
items.statement: For f:X→S proper and F coherent, a point s∈S has the natural map φ^q_s:(R^qf_*F)⊗_{O_S}κ(s)→H^q(X_s,F_s), induced by restriction to the fibre and derived direct image. For S′→S there is likewise g^*R^qf_*F→R^qf′_*g′*F. These maps are not asserted isomorphisms without further hypotheses.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.title: Finite-free local criterion for base change
items.statement: For a bounded finite-free cochain complex K over any local ring (A,m) with residue field κ, the natural map H^q(K)⊗κ→H^q(K⊗κ) is surjective iff, after shrinking Spec A around m, d^q has a split constant-rank matrix form. Under this condition H^q(K⊗A′)=H^q(K)⊗A′ for every A-algebra A′ on that neighbourhood; H^q(K) is locally free iff the analogous map in degree q−1 is also surjective, with degree −1 interpreted as automatic.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2
The Stacks Project, Derived Categories of Schemes, §§36.26–36.32

items.strategy: Choose a maximal-size nonzero minor of d^q on the residue-field complex, invert it near m, and split an identity block. The residual differential D has all entries in m. Its preceding differential lands in ker D. Surjectivity of φ^q says every class in the residual fibre kernel has a genuine lifted cycle modulo a fibre boundary. Lifts of boundaries are already cycles, so the lifted cycles generate the residual free source modulo m. Nakayama on its finite free quotient forces them to generate near m, hence D=0 there. Conversely if D=0, cycles are a fixed free summand and right exactness of cokernels gives H^q(K⊗A′)=H^q(K)⊗A′ for every A′. Given this splitting, H^q is the cokernel of d^{q−1} into the free cycle summand. It is locally free iff the image is a direct summand, equivalently the same residue-field surjectivity test in degree q−1. This is the matrix argument of Vakil §28.2.10–11; finite rank and Nakayama suffice over an arbitrary local ring.

items.title: Cohomology and base change for proper flat coherent families
items.statement: Let f:X→S be proper and of finite presentation, with S arbitrary, and F coherent (in particular finitely presented) on X and flat over S. At s∈S, if φ^q_s is surjective, then on some neighbourhood U of s every base change T→U makes g^*(R^qf_*F)→R^qf_T*F_T an isomorphism; moreover R^qf_*F is locally free near s iff φ^{q−1}_s is surjective (automatic for q=0). In particular φ^q_s itself is then an isomorphism.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2
The Stacks Project, Derived Categories of Schemes, §§36.26–36.32

items.strategy: Work on an arbitrary affine neighbourhood Spec A of s; coherent F is finitely presented under the stated convention. Use the universal bounded finite projective complex from Noetherian approximation, then localize so its terms are finite free. Identify φ^q_s with the cohomology-to-fibre map of this complex. The finite-free matrix criterion gives a neighbourhood on which the degree-q cohomology commutes with every ring base change, and the adjacent-degree criterion gives local freeness. The local derived complexes and the canonical natural base-change maps agree under further restriction, so the affine results glue for any T→U. No Noetherian assumption remains in the conclusion.

items.title: Upper semicontinuity of fibre cohomology
items.statement: For f:X→S proper of finite presentation and F a coherent S-flat sheaf, s↦dim_{κ(s)}H^q(X_s,F_s) is upper semicontinuous for every q, with no Noetherian assumption on S.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2
The Stacks Project, Derived Categories of Schemes, §§36.26–36.32

items.strategy: Locally use the universal finite-free complex K. On a fibre, h^q=rank K^q−rank d^{q−1}−rank d^q. Each matrix rank is lower semicontinuous because rank≥r is an open condition defined by the nonvanishing of an r-minor. Hence h^q is upper semicontinuous. This computes the fibre groups even at jump points where ordinary cohomology base change is not an isomorphism; Stacks §36.32 Lemma 32.1 confirms the arbitrary-base scope.

items.title: Euler characteristic in a proper flat family is locally constant
items.statement: Let f:X→S be proper of finite presentation, with S arbitrary, and F coherent and flat over S. Then χ(X_s,F_s)=Σ_q(−1)^q dim_{κ(s)}H^q(X_s,F_s) is locally constant on S. If f is flat, this applies to F=O_X.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2
The Stacks Project, Derived Categories of Schemes, §§36.26–36.32

items.strategy: On each affine neighbourhood use its universal bounded finite-projective complex K. For every fibre the alternating sum of cohomology dimensions equals the alternating sum of the ranks of K^q⊗κ(s), since boundaries cancel in a finite complex. Finite-projective ranks are locally constant, so χ is locally constant. The sheaf must be S-flat; the final structure-sheaf case uses flatness of f.

items.title: Hypersurface cohomology sequence
items.statement: For a field k, nonzero homogeneous f∈k[x_0,…,x_n] of degree d>0, and X=V_+(f)⊂P^n_k, the exact sequence 0→O_{P^n}(-d) --f→ O_{P^n}→i_*O_X→0 yields the long exact cohomology sequence, computing H^q(X,O_X) from the explicit projective-space groups. More generally the same holds over a ring when f is a nonzerodivisor on O_{P^n}.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: On each standard affine chart, f dehomogenizes to a nonzerodivisor over a field (since the polynomial ring is a domain); over a general base require the displayed nonzerodivisor hypothesis. Thus multiplication by f is injective and its cokernel is the structure sheaf of the closed hypersurface. Apply the published long exact sequence and the closed-immersion cohomology isomorphism. Keep n=0 and empty hypersurface consistent.

items.title: Global functions on geometrically connected and geometrically reduced proper schemes
items.statement: If X is a nonempty proper geometrically connected and geometrically reduced k-scheme, then H^0(X,O_X)=k. Geometric reducedness cannot be replaced by reducedness over k.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Proper coherent finiteness makes B=Γ(X,O_X) a finite-dimensional k-algebra. Flat field extension gives B⊗_k kbar=Γ(X_kbar,O), where kbar is an algebraic closure. Geometric reducedness makes this finite algebra reduced; over algebraically closed kbar it is a finite product of kbar. Geometric connectedness rules out nontrivial idempotents, so the product has exactly one factor and dimension one. Hence dim_k B=1 and the unit k→B is an isomorphism. For the warning, a purely inseparable nontrivial field extension L/k gives Spec L reduced and proper with H0=L but X_kbar nonreduced. AC is used only to choose the algebraic closure; the finite-algebra argument itself is elementary.

items.title: Coherence is essential for proper finiteness
items.statement: Even on proper P^1_k, a quasi-coherent sheaf such as ⊕_{m≥1}O_{P^1} has infinite-dimensional H^0; the proper pushforward finiteness theorem is a coherent-sheaf assertion.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

title: Cohomology of Quasi Coherent Sheaves on Affine and Projective Schemes — Examples

items.title: All twists on the projective line
items.statement: For a field k and d∈Z, h^0(P^1_k,O(d))=max(d+1,0), h^1(P^1_k,O(d))=max(−d−1,0), and χ=d+1.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Use the standard two-chart complex k[z]z^d⊕k[z^{-1}]→k[z,z^{-1}] with the O(d) transition. Its degree-zero monomials are x_0^{d-j}x_1^j for 0≤j≤d when d≥0. Its H1 basis is x_0^{-a}x_1^{-b} with a,b≥1 and a+b=−d when d≤−2, giving −d−1 elements. The middle case d=−1 has neither group. Subtract dimensions to get χ=d+1 in all cases.

items.title: Generator cocycle for H1 of O(-2)
items.statement: On P^1_k covered by D_+(x_0),D_+(x_1), the class of 1/(x_0x_1) in the overlap section of O(-2) spans H^1(P^1_k,O(-2))≅k.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Write the two-chart Čech quotient explicitly. The Laurent monomial x_0^{-1}x_1^{-1} has negative exponent in both variables, so it appears only in the overlap summand and cannot come from either chart. Every other degree −2 Laurent monomial is regular on at least one chart, hence is a boundary. Thus the quotient is one-dimensional on the displayed class.

items.title: Plane cubic structure-sheaf cohomology
items.statement: For any nonzero homogeneous cubic f∈k[x_0,x_1,x_2] and C=V_+(f)⊂P^2_k, H^0(C,O_C)≅k and H^1(C,O_C)≅k, with all higher groups zero. Smoothness is unnecessary.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Use 0→O_{P2}(-3)→O_{P2}→i_*O_C→0. The projective-space formula gives H0 O(-3)=0, H1 of either twist=0, H2 O=0 and H2 O(-3)=k generated by (x0x1x2)^{-1}. The long exact sequence therefore identifies H0 O_C with k and H1 O_C with k; the Čech dimension bound kills higher degrees.

items.title: Hilbert polynomial of projective space
items.statement: For P^n_k and its standard O(1), P_{O}(m)=χ(P^n_k,O(m))=binomial(m+n,n) as a polynomial in every integer m, and for m≥0 it equals h^0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: For m≥0 count nonnegative monomials to get binomial(m+n,n). For −n≤m<0 the Euler characteristic and the polynomial both vanish (when n>0). For m≤−n−1 only H^n survives with dimension binomial(−m−1,n); its sign (−1)^n turns this into binomial(m+n,n). When n=0, P0=Spec k gives χ=1 and the polynomial is identically 1.

items.title: h0 differs from Euler characteristic before vanishing
items.statement: For O_{P^1_k}(−2), h^0=0 while χ=−1 because h^1=1. Thus the Hilbert function need not equal the Hilbert polynomial at negative twists.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Insert d=−2 in the all-twists calculation: H0=0, H1=k. The alternating sum is −1, while the degree-zero dimension is zero. This witnesses the missing higher-cohomology term without contradicting eventual Serre vanishing.

items.title: A non-quasi-coherent module with H1 on an affine scheme
items.statement: Assume AC. Let k be any field, A=k[t], X=Spec A, Z={V(t),V(t−1)}, U=X\Z, and j:U→X. The extension by zero F=j_!(O_U), with its natural O_X-module structure, is not quasi-coherent and has H^1(X,F)≅(A_(t)×A_(t−1))/diagonal(A)≠0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The usual extension-by-zero sheaf j_!O_U is an O_X-module: multiplication by a local O_X section preserves the support condition, and the canonical map j_!O_U→O_X is O_X-linear. Apply the published open/closed-complement exact sequence to the underlying abelian sheaf, giving 0→j_!O_U→O_X→i_*i^{-1}O_X→0. The two-point closed subspace Z is discrete, so Γ(X,i_*i^{-1}O_X)=O_{X,(t)}×O_{X,(t−1)}=A_(t)×A_(t−1). Affine acyclicity gives H^1(X,O_X)=0, and the long exact sequence identifies H^1(X,F) with the displayed cokernel of Γ(X,O_X)=A. The class of (0,1) is nonzero because A→A_(t) is injective: a polynomial whose germ at (t) is zero must be zero and cannot map to 1 at (t−1). If F were quasi-coherent, the affine vanishing theorem would force H^1(X,F)=0. Thus the same O_X-module violates affine acyclicity exactly when quasi-coherence is removed.

items.title: Proper cohomology need not be finite for noncoherent sheaves
items.statement: On proper P^1_k, the quasi-coherent but noncoherent F=⊕_{r≥1}O_{P^1_k} has H^0(P^1_k,F)≅⊕_{r≥1}k, which is infinite-dimensional.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The finite two-affine Čech complex for F is the direct sum of the complexes for each O summand, because localization and finite direct sums commute with arbitrary module sums. Cohomology in degree zero therefore commutes with this sum and gives a countable direct sum of k. Every stalk has infinite rank, so F is not finite type and hence not coherent on Noetherian P1.

items.title: An upper jump of h0 in a flat projective family
items.statement: Over S=Spec k[a], there is a rank-two vector bundle E on P^1_S fitting into 0→O(−2)→E→O→0 with extension cocycle a/(x_0x_1). On the fibre a=0, h^0(E_0)=1; on every fibre a≠0, h^0(E_a)=0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Construct E by gluing frames (u0,v0) and (u1,v1) on the standard charts using u1=z^{−2}u0 and v1=v0+a z^{−1}u0, where z=x1/x0; determinant z^{−2} is invertible on the overlap, so E is locally free and S-flat. The quotient v_i mod u_i is the unit frame of O. The connecting map H0(O)=κ(s)→H1(O(−2))=κ(s) sends 1 to a times the generator, so is zero at a=0 and an isomorphism otherwise. Since H0(O(−2))=0, its kernel is exactly H0(E_s), giving the displayed jump.

items.title: Compensating h0 and h1 jumps with constant Euler characteristic
items.statement: For the rank-two S-flat bundle E in the preceding gluing construction, (h^0,h^1)(E_0)=(1,1) and (h^0,h^1)(E_s)=(0,0) for a(s)≠0; χ(E_s)=0 on every fibre.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Use the long exact sequence of 0→O(−2)→E_s→O→0 and the explicit connecting map multiplication by a(s). Both the domain H0(O) and target H1(O(−2)) are one-dimensional; its kernel is H0(E_s) and cokernel is H1(E_s), because the other boundary groups vanish. At a=0 they each have dimension one; elsewhere both are zero. Their alternating sum is always zero, agreeing with the proper flat family corollary.

items.title: Projective zero-space over an affine base
items.statement: For any ring A, P^0_A≅Spec A and O_{P^0_A}(d)≅O_{Spec A} for all d∈Z; hence H^0≅A and H^q=0 for q>0. For a nonaffine base S, P^0_S≅S and no general higher-cohomology vanishing is asserted.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: Proj A[x0] has one standard chart D_+(x0)=Spec A; its degree-d localization piece is free rank one on x0^d, even for negative d. The scheme and twist identifications reduce cohomology to affine acyclicity. For general S the relative Proj local charts glue to S, so the last sentence only identifies spaces and avoids an erroneous nonaffine vanishing claim.

items.title: A nonseparated affine cover can have nonaffine intersection
items.statement: Glue two copies of A^2_k along A^2_k minus {0}. The resulting nonseparated scheme X has an affine two-open cover, but its intersection U=A^2_k minus {0} is not affine; indeed H^1(U,O_U) contains the nonzero Čech class x^{−1}y^{−1}.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2

items.strategy: The overlap U is covered by affine D(x),D(y) with affine D(xy) intersection. Its degree-one Čech quotient is k[x^{±1},y^{±1}]/(k[x^{±1},y]+k[x,y^{±1}]); the Laurent monomial x^{−1}y^{−1} survives because it has negative exponents in both variables. Therefore H1(U,O_U)≠0, so U cannot be affine by affine acyclicity. The two glued A2 charts give the advertised affine cover; the failure of affine intersection also violates the affine diagonal criterion and shows why the separated hypothesis is used.

items.title: Base change requires its actual map and hypotheses
items.statement: The map (R^qf_*F)⊗κ(s)→H^q(X_s,F_s) can fail to be an isomorphism even in a proper flat family with F flat; fibre dimensions can jump. The local criterion must be checked at the specified degree, and local freeness uses the adjacent degree.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Chapter 30, §§30.2–30.22
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (29 August 2022), §§19.1, 19.6, 19.9, 28.1–28.2
